subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class pre-compaction lifecycle contract with configurable threshold warnings, a structured handoff turn, and bounded deferral authority, or should current main stay limited to hooks, memoryFlush, notices, and checkpoint branch/restore APIs?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested deferral and checkpoint semantics decide how session state, tool authority, approvals, and policy scope survive a compaction boundary; automation cannot choose that product/security contract safely.

options.title: Design The Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Approve a design pass that specifies thresholds, handoff capabilities, deferral limits, audit records, authority checks, defaults, and how existing hooks/checkpoints are reused before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Surfaces
options.body: Limit follow-up work to documenting or extending current hook messages, memoryFlush, notifyUser, and checkpoint branch/restore APIs without adding deferral authority.

options.title: Defer New Compaction Controls
options.body: Keep current behavior and close or pause this direction until maintainers see stronger evidence that the existing memoryFlush/checkpoint/notifier stack is insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design The Lifecycle Contract First
recommendation.body: Approve a design pass that specifies thresholds, handoff capabilities, deferral limits, audit records, authority checks, defaults, and how existing hooks/checkpoints are reused before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored follow-up fixes in the adjacent compaction visibility path and is the strongest available routing signal for the product/security lifecycle decision.
